prompt:
Write a clinical treatment summary (about 150 words) by the treating provider for a patient with knee injury after a rear-end collision. The patient had 28 visits. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1158; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Some exam findings support the injury; other tests are normal.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- The bills show no repeated charges.
text: Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with ongoing right knee pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion. Over the course of 28 visits, care consisted of physical examination, imaging review, a structured physical therapy program, and home exercise instruction. The reported knee complaints are consistent with the mechanism and force of the collision as described in the history. Early visits were frequent, and the treatment intensity tapered steadily as symptoms improved and function returned. Some examination findings, including joint line tenderness and a positive effusion sign, support the presence of a knee injury. Other tests, including ligament stability assessments and neurovascular checks, were within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment involving this body area is known from the patient's history or records. Billed services reflect the care delivered, with no duplicated or repeated charges identified. The patient is currently improving and is expected to continue a home program with periodic follow-up as needed.
